info.title: Goosy Bear API
info.summary: Manage workspace content, projects, Data tables, Pages, library and credits.
info.description: BETA. This API is in beta: paths, request shapes and response envelopes may change, and every response carries an `x-goosy-api: beta` header for as long as that is true. A change is additive, or it is deprecated first: a response to a call that uses a deprecated feature carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers, and nothing is removed until at least 90 days after its deprecation. Pin the OpenAPI document you generated against and re-generate when it changes.

post.description:
Read where this workspace's content stands — 'what's scheduled this week?', 'why did that post fail?' — every piece with its lifecycle status, its schedule, its elected platform versions, and the reason any of it failed. Call this before answering any question about what is drafted, ready, scheduled or live; never guess it. It reads only. Not for the week laid out by day — that is `schedule.read`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

workspace.description: Which workspace to run in — its slug. Omit to use your default. With more than one reachable workspace and no default, the call is refused and the choices are listed.

post.description:
Search this workspace's library — 'do we have a photo of the storefront?', 'find last month's launch video' — every finished image, clip, video and document, with the pinned ones first. Call this before answering any question about what this brand already has; never guess whether an asset exists. It reads only. Not for reading one item you already have the id of — that is `library.get`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Create a typed Data table in this workspace and place it on a board — 'make a table to track sponsors', 'set up a list of our venues'. It goes on the board you name, or on a new board made through the canonical board creator. Not for adding rows — that is `data.api_append`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Your key for this write: send the same key when you retry and the first result comes back instead of a second action. Keys are honoured for at least 24 hours. 1–200 visible ASCII characters. Replaces the `idempotency_key` body field, which still works until 2026-12-31; this action needs a key on one of the two, and the header is the one to send.

name.description: What this table is called, in the operator's own words.

key.description: The column's identifier: lower snake case, starting with a letter, at most 64 characters (for example `first_name`). It is what row values are keyed by.

post.description:
Propose, then confirm, making one page of a site members-only — so only signed-in members of the workspace can open it — or public again: 'make the team page private', 'open /pricing to everyone again'. A live site rebuilds and publishes itself with the change; a draft site's change lands with its next build. It sets one page by its path, never a pattern such as '/admin/*' — relay that refusal, which says a pattern is edited in the site's source. Not for publishing a built version — that is `page.api_publish`.

post.description:
Write a small custom card for this workspace — 'build me a calculator for this', 'make a countdown to the launch' — a little self-contained page, coded from the brief you give it, rendered in a sandbox and readable at its own address. Use it when what is wanted is not one of the ordinary elements: a bespoke view, a calculator, a countdown, a table shaped a particular way. Carry the operator's own sentence into brief; it is the whole instruction the card is written from. If the card needs live data, pass every Data table it may read in data_table_ids — a table you do not pass is a table the card can never see. post.description:
Create every post a brief calls for, in one call — 'make this week's posts from Tuesday's episode', 'create three posts for the launch'. Each piece is created with whatever the request already settles — what it is built from, where it goes, its own copy, its time — and gets its board, so a complete request needs no further calls beyond each destination's version. Read posts.plan_context first so slot ids, library ids and destination names are real. It creates drafts only: nothing is published or sent for approval. Not for reading where one piece stands afterwards — that is `posts.api_read_piece`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Your key for this write: send the same key when you retry and the first result comes back instead of a second action. Keys are honoured for at least 24 hours. 1–200 visible ASCII characters. Replaces the `idempotency_key` body field, which still works until 2026-12-31; this action needs a key on one of the two, and the header is the one to send.

title.description: What the operator would call this piece. Short and human — it labels the tile on their grid.

schedule_slot_id.description: The open cadence slot from posts.plan_context this piece fills. PREFER THIS: the slot supplies the destinations AND the time, so passing it means you do not pass `platforms` or `scheduled_for` at all. Omit only for a genuinely ad-hoc piece the cadence has no slot for.

platforms.description: Where this piece publishes. Omit when `schedule_slot_id` is set — the slot's own defaults are the operator's rhythm and restating them is what drifts. Pass ONLY values posts.plan_context listed as electable; anything else is refused.

master_content.description: The piece's own copy — the canonical version every destination's variant is shaped from. Write it here when the brief gives you enough to; otherwise omit and fill it later with posts.fill_step.

source_kind.description: What this piece is built from. Use `video_unit` with the id from posts.plan_context's finals list when the brief names an episode. `scratch` (the default) means written in the flow and takes NO source_ref.

source_ref.description: The id of the final named by `source_kind`. Required for every kind but `scratch`, and forbidden for `scratch`.

scheduled_for.description: When this piece goes out, ISO 8601 UTC. Omit when `schedule_slot_id` is set. Convert the operator's wall-clock intent using the `displayTimeZone` posts.plan_context returned — never assume UTC is their zone.

pieces.description: Every piece the brief asks for, in ONE call. A week of posts is one call, not one call per post.

idempotency_key.description: Deprecated on REST: send the `Idempotency-Key` header instead. Still accepted until 2026-12-31; if both are sent they must match.

workspace.description: Which workspace to run in — its slug. Omit to use your default. With more than one reachable workspace and no default, the call is refused and the choices are listed.

post.description:
Save the version written for each destination of a post — 'save these captions for Instagram and LinkedIn', 'here's the LinkedIn version of this post'. It stores the words you send; it writes none itself. A destination must already be on the piece, each version must carry its words, and a destination that already published refuses, because its copy is the record of what went out. It saves the draft only; nothing is published. Not for the piece's own copy — that is `posts.api_fill_step`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Your key for this write: send the same key when you retry and the first result comes back instead of a second action. Keys are honoured for at least 24 hours. 1–200 visible ASCII characters. Replaces the `idempotency_key` body field, which still works until 2026-12-31; this action needs a key on one of the two, and the header is the one to send.

piece_id.description: The piece's id, as posts.create_pieces, content.create_request, content.status or schedule.read return it.

platform.description: The destination this version is for. Must already be elected.

caption.description: This destination's version of the copy — what actually posts there.

description.description: The longer body, for destinations that have one (a YouTube description, a Google Business post). Omit where the destination only has a caption.

publish_at.description: This destination's OWN time, ISO 8601 UTC — a per-platform offset from the piece's anchor. Omit unless the brief asked for one; the piece's own time covers every destination that has none.

aspect_ratio.description: Override the managed default aspect for this destination. Omit unless the operator asked — the default is the managed configuration and is nearly always right.

hashtags.description: The tags going out with THIS destination's version. Write them WITHOUT the leading # — the surface adds it, so a stored one doubles it. One word each, no spaces.

alt_text.description: What the creative SHOWS, for a reader who cannot see it — the subject, what they are doing, the setting. Describe the image, never repeat the caption.

first_comment.description: The comment posted immediately behind the piece, where the destination has the convention. Omit on destinations that do not.

location_label.description: The place this post is tagged at, as a human label ("Northwind Trading Co. · Portland, OR"). Never invent one the operator has not given you.

tagged_handles.description: The accounts tagged in this destination's version, WITHOUT the leading @. Only accounts the operator named — a tagged account is a claim about someone else.

text_sticker.description: The white pill laid over this frame's picture. A short line, not a caption — omit it where the picture speaks for itself.

link_sticker_url.description: Where this frame's link sticker sends a viewer. Only a destination the operator named.

link_sticker_label.description: The words ON the link pill ("See the menu"). Ignored without link_sticker_url — a label with no destination is a pill that goes nowhere.

music_label.description: The track as the platform NAMES it ("Golden Hour · JVKE"). Only a track the operator picked — never one you chose for them.

alt_text.description: What THIS frame's picture shows, for a reader who cannot see it. Per frame — three frames are three different pictures.

poll.description: The poll sticker on this frame. A question with two to four options; anything less is a question, not a poll.

mention_handles.description: Accounts @-mentioned ON this frame, WITHOUT the leading @ — the surface adds it. Only accounts the operator named.

duration_seconds.description: How long this frame sits on screen. Omit for the platforms' own 5-second still.

frames.description: EVERY frame of this story, in order — the first entry is the frame a viewer sees first. This REPLACES the whole rail: any frame you do not list is removed.

expires_at.description: When the story stops being visible, ISO 8601 UTC. Normally 24 hours after it posts; omit unless the operator said otherwise.

highlight_name.description: The highlight the story is saved into after it expires. Only one the operator named.

replies_mode.description: WHO MAY REPLY to the story. Omit to leave the account's own default — never guess it.

story.description: Only on a stories piece: every frame of this destination's story, in order, plus when it expires, the highlight it is saved to and who may reply. Including this REPLACES the whole rail.

variants.description: Every destination's version, in ONE call. Each one must carry the words — a destination with only its name on it is refused, because there is nothing to put on the piece.

post.description:
Put a film already recorded onto a story that was waiting for one — 'use this clip for that story', 'attach my recording to this story'. The story stops waiting and its words are written over the film by a drafting run, which is model work charged to the workspace. A story that already has its take is left as it is. Not for trimming the film or changing its look: that is done in Videos, and no verb here does it. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Send a finished post for approval — 'send this post for approval', 'submit this for review'. Read it with posts.read_piece first: a piece with steps still outstanding, no destinations, or withdrawn content is refused, and the refusal names why. This submits only; the approval itself is always a person's, in Reviews or on the piece, and nothing goes out without that approval. Not for setting when it goes out — that is `posts.set_schedule`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Your key for this write: send the same key when you retry and the first result comes back instead of a second action. Keys are honoured for at least 24 hours. 1–200 visible ASCII characters. Replaces the `idempotency_key` body field, which still works until 2026-12-31; this action needs a key on one of the two, and the header is the one to send.

piece_id.description: The piece's id, as posts.create_pieces, content.create_request, content.status or schedule.read return it.

idempotency_key.description: Deprecated on REST: send the `Idempotency-Key` header instead. Still accepted until 2026-12-31; if both are sent they must match.

workspace.description: Which workspace to run in — its slug. Omit to use your default. With more than one reachable workspace and no default, the call is refused and the choices are listed.

200.description: The call was admitted and dispatched. `ok` says whether the tool succeeded — a refusal the tool itself produced is still a 200, exactly as it is a successful JSON-RPC result over MCP.

post.description:
'write the script for this video', 'rewrite the script to be more casual' — write one video's script from its plan, or rewrite it under one direction you pass. The answer carries the chapters and any facts the script still needs. This runs a PAID writing turn: on a member's own key it writes in one call; on a key with no member behind it the first call describes what would be written, charges nothing and returns a confirmation id, and the second, carrying that id back, is what writes it. Not for drawing the scenes — that is `videos.draw_storyboard`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'edit this video', 'make it tighter', 'cut scene three shorter' — edit one video, optionally under a direction or for one scene, and return the log of what changed — or, if the edit is still running when this answers, state in_flight and a job_id to follow with `jobs.read` (do not send it again). A retry carrying the same idempotency_key is the same edit. This runs a PAID editing turn: on a member's own key it edits in one call; on a key with no member behind it the first call describes the edit, charges nothing and returns a confirmation id, and the second, carrying that id back, is what edits it. Not for reading an edit already made — that is `videos.read_edit`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'send my completed jobs to this URL', 'notify our server when a clip is done' — register the workspace's job-completion webhook, or replace it: the https URL to announce completed jobs to, and a signing secret the operator chose and keeps. Once set, every long-running job that finishes (a clip from videos.generate_clip, an edit or draft that answered in_flight) is announced once, as a POST signed with that secret whose body is the job's jobs.read answer. The secret is never shown back. It spends nothing and starts no job. Not for reading a job's status — that is jobs.read.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.name: x-request-id
parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

url.description: The https URL to announce completed jobs to. It must name a public host on the default port, with no user name, password or fragment.

post.description:
'what images are on this board', 'tell me more about this image' — without generation_id, list one board's images, newest first: each image's id, stored caption and status; with generation_id, read that one image's stored description in full. The board is named by id and must be this workspace's. A listing is one page: totalCount is the board's real size, hasMore means older images sit on later pages, and page is a direct index, so the oldest images are on page ceil(totalCount / pageSize). It changes nothing. Not for the workspace's saved photos, logo and product shots — that is `images.brand_elements`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

generation_id.description: The id of ONE image to describe in detail. OMIT to list this board's images (ids + prompts + captions) — call it that way FIRST whenever you need an image id for images.iterate / images.add_to_board.

page.description: Listing page, a DIRECT INDEX (newest first, 8 per page) — page 1 is the newest and the OLDEST images are on page ceil(totalCount / pageSize), so jump straight to the page you want rather than walking one page at a time. The listing result says totalCount and hasMore. Ignored when generation_id is set.

board.description: The board to act on, by id — one of this workspace's boards (board.tree lists them).

The name is required; saving the same image twice changes nothing and the answer says it was already a style. Not for keeping the image itself in the Library — that is `images.save_to_library`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

generation_id.description: The id of the image whose LOOK should be saved.

name.description: What to call the style — REQUIRED, because this is how the operator picks it later. Use their words if they named it; otherwise propose a short descriptive name and say what you chose.

note.description: Optional 'when to use this' note for the operator's own reference.

board.description: Optional: the board this image is being saved from, by id — recorded as where it came from. Omit when there is none.

workspace.description: Which workspace to run in — its slug. Omit to use your default. With more than one reachable workspace and no default, the call is refused and the choices are listed.

200.description: The call was admitted and dispatched. `ok` says whether the tool succeeded — a refusal the tool itself produced is still a 200, exactly as it is a successful JSON-RPC result over MCP.

post.description:
'what automations do we have?', 'is that automation still on?' — list this workspace's automations, the same rows its Automations board shows: each one's definition id, name, status (Running, Needs a look, Paused or Not scheduled), the project it lives in, its schedule in words, when it last ran and when it fires next, plus a count per status. It answers one page — as many automations as fit, in the board's order — and `counts` on every page covers every automation, not only the rows shown; when `next_cursor` comes back, call again with it as `cursor` for the rest, and `limit` asks for fewer. It changes nothing. Not for whether one automation's inbound webhook is set up — that is `automations.webhook_token_status`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

'what's our one-liner?', 'which offer is running right now?', 'find the photo of Alex at the counter' — read this workspace's brand kit: who the brand is, what it offers, who it is for, how it sounds and looks, where it is, its video settings, and its pictures by label, kind and tag (never the files). Each fact says whether a member confirmed it or it is still a suggestion; a suggestion carries the fact_id and updated_at a member confirms on the brand page. A large kit comes back in part, with `omitted` naming the groups to read next by `group`. It changes nothing. Not for adding or correcting a fact — that is `brand_kit.suggest`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'we're running a Harvest Week sale, 1 to 7 October', 'add our new shop on Alder Street' — add one fact to this workspace's brand kit as a SUGGESTION: a location, an offer, a person, a picture and its name, a contact detail, a product. `kind` is the kit's own name for the fact (read the kit first when unsure); a kind the kit holds many of takes an `item_key`. It never confirms anything and never overwrites a confirmed fact: a change waits beside it until a member confirms it on the brand page. The same suggestion twice changes nothing. A dated note (kind `timing`) is refused with `brand_kit.note_chat_only`: a member says it in chat, and the API has no speaker to own it. Not for how closely drafts follow the brand — that is `brand_kit.set_adherence`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'make us a logo', 'make the icon set from our logo', 'make some poses of Alex' — run one of this workspace's brand playbooks: poses of one of the brand's people, a logo pack (a logo with its favicon and icon set), or the icon set from the logo the brand has. It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it returns the price per stage and a confirmation_id and spends nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, starts the run, spends the quoted credits and answers its job_run_id. The logo pack pauses after drawing its directions: a call without confirmation_id then answers `awaiting_pick`, and choosing one (`pick`) takes the same two calls and spends nothing. Not for a single picture or an edit to one — that is `images.generate`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

'find a real shot for this scene', 'use a real clip of a desk here' — find a real-world shot for one storyboard scene and drop it in as an insert of a few seconds; it never replaces the scene, and the answer names who took it with a link. It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it says what would be looked for and for how long, and searches nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, searches, keeps the shot in this workspace's clips and places it. post.description:
'pause this automation's schedule', 'stop it running on schedule for now' — stop one automation in this workspace, named by its board_id, from running on its schedule, without switching the automation off. It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes, shows the schedule as it stands and changes nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, pauses it. Not for switching the whole automation off — that is `automations.deactivate`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'test this automation', 'dry-run it before we switch it on' — dry-run one automation in this workspace, named by its board_id, against the workspace's synthetic test contact: its draft (or, with no draft, the version that runs) walks every step, sends go only to the workspace's designated test address, waits are skipped and CRM writes are withheld. A run uses model and step time. It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes, names the version and the test address and runs nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, runs it. Not for switching it on for real contacts — that is `automations.activate`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'why did the email step fail?', 'fix the step that broke on the last run' — repair ONE step of an automation in this workspace, named by its board_id, that failed on its last run. With just step_key it reads how that step failed and how it is configured today, and changes nothing. With a fix it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes the change and shows that one step before and after, changing nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, saves it as a new draft that does not run until it is switched on. A fix that would touch any other step, the order or what starts the automation is refused. Not for rewriting the whole automation — that is `automations.author`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'rotate that webhook token', 'give me a new token for the Zapier trigger' — replace the inbound webhook token of one webhook-triggered automation in this workspace, named by its definition_id (automations.list gives it). It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes, says whether a token exists and whether the automation is live, and changes nothing; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, rotates it and returns the new token ONCE, in that answer — store it then, nothing can show it again, and every sender on the old token is refused from that moment. Needs an account admin's key. With intent `mint` it issues an automation's FIRST token the same way. Not for shutting a webhook off — that is `automations.revoke_webhook_token`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
'yes, that address is right — confirm it', 'confirm the Harvest Week offer' — confirm ONE suggested fact in this workspace's brand kit exactly as a member was shown it: the fact's id and the updated_at `brand_kit.read` returned; it takes no value. It answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes and shows the fact as it would be confirmed; the same call again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, starts the confirm and answers its job_run_id — the confirm runs on its own, in seconds. A suggestion that changed since it was read is refused. Not for changing a fact — that is `brand_kit.suggest` with the corrected value, then a confirm of that new version.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Find domain names the member could buy and what each costs — 'what domains are available?', 'is mybrand.com free?', 'find me a good name for this'. Find domain names the customer could buy, with what each costs per year. Every name is for ONE year and renews at the same kind of price — there is no first-year discount that jumps later. Read the price back before anyone commits to anything, and note that a name marked premium costs more to renew as well. This only looks; it never buys. Not for getting a name ready to buy — that is `domain.purchase`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Not for pointing a domain at a site — that is `domain.connect`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Move a domain the member already has onto a different site — 'point mydomain.com at the new page instead', 'move my domain to this site', 'that address should go somewhere else now'. Move one of the customer's domains onto a different page. If serving_now comes back false the address is assigned but nothing is being served on it yet — read revision to tell which case it is. revision null: the page has never been published, so say that and offer to publish. revision set: this is a name we bought for the customer and it is not answering on the internet yet, so say that instead and never blame the page. Either way, do not call it live. The address we gave a page (its goosydoes.com name) belongs to that page and cannot be moved. Not for connecting a domain for the first time — that is `domain.connect`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

post.description:
Give the member the steps to move a domain we bought them to another registrar — 'I want to move my domain elsewhere', 'how do I transfer this out?', 'get me the auth code'. Give the customer the exact steps to move a domain we registered for them to another registrar, and say whether it may leave yet. We can't do the move for them — the unlock and the authorization code are done in the registrar's own dashboard — so relay guided_step in order. Relay the eligibility reason WORD FOR WORD: eligible means no hold is visible from the registration date, NOT a guarantee the transfer will be accepted. This prepares only; nothing is transferred by this call. Not for pointing it at another site here — that is `domain.point_at_site`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Do something through a site's own backend — 'save that through the site's admin', 'add a record the way the site does it', 'hit my site's own API for me'.  Call one of this site's OWN routes — its admin save route, its API — signed in as the member, exactly as their browser would. Use it to operate a site's own backend: add a record, change a setting, read an admin listing. The path is site-local and starts with a slash; the site decides what each route does, so read the site's code or ask the member rather than guessing a route or a body shape. A members-only route is reachable this way and no other way from chat. A GET runs straight away; a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE changes the live site, so the member sees the method, the path and the site on a card and approves it before anything is sent. Not for reading or changing the site's own database — that is `site.database.query` or `site.database.execute`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Look inside a site's own database — 'what's in my site's database?', 'how many bookings are stored?', 'show me the products the site has'.  Read this site's own database with one read-only SQL statement. It is the site's whole schema — the same database the site's own code reads as env.DB — so start with `select name from sqlite_master where type='table'` if you do not know it. Put every value in `params` as a ? placeholder. The statement must start with select, with, explain, or pragma table_info / table_list and carry no semicolon: this tool REFUSES anything that could change data or schema. Not for changing data or schema — that is `site.database.execute`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Change what a site's own database holds — 'add that product to my site's shop', 'update the price in the site's database', 'delete that stale record from the site'.  Change this site's own database with one SQL statement — insert, update, delete, or a schema change the site's code expects. Calling it raises the approval card showing the exact statement — and, for an update or delete, how many rows it touches — which is the member's confirmation. Put every value in `params` as a ? placeholder, and read the schema with site.database.query before writing. post.description:
List this workspace's customer pages — name, draft/live status, address, last activity and lead count — plus the workspace totals (total_count, live_count, leads_this_month). The reply is ONE PAGE of sites, newest activity first: when it carries next_cursor there are more, so say how many you showed of total_count and pass next_cursor as cursor to read the next page (if the sites changed in between, the cursor is refused: start again from the first page and read the list over rather than joining it to what you have). Pass list 'templates' to read the template catalogue instead — the first-party template ids page.create accepts and every saved template this account can start from, named so you can offer them by name, also one page at a time. That template list is WIDER than this workspace: some were published by other workspaces in the same account and some are ours and shipped to every account — each row says which (`scope`), whether this workspace authored it (`owned_by_this_workspace`), and whether you may withdraw it (`retirable`). Only a row with `retirable: true` can be retired here. Reach for sites when the member asks WHICH sites they have — 'what pages do I have?', 'show me my sites', 'is the pricing page live yet?' — or when they name a site that is NOT the one already open on screen and you need its id; reach for templates only before offering a template by name. Not for one site's own state — that is `page.read` — and not for finding the site already open on their screen: that surface already carries its id, and listing the workspace to rediscover it is the hunt that ends in the wrong id.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Show which FILES a site is actually built from — 'what files does this site have?', 'show me the code', 'which file is the hero in?', 'where does the pricing copy live?'. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. Reach for it to find where something lives before changing it, or when the member wants to see the source itself. It is the same tree the Files board shows, for every site whose files we hold, however it was made or brought in. A site we hold no source for answers kind: no_source_snapshot; say so rather than inventing files. A BIG PROJECT ANSWERS IN PAGES: total is the real file count, and when more files follow the result carries next_cursor — call again with cursor: next_cursor and the same path_prefix and contains to read on (if the site's files changed in between, the cursor is refused: start again from the first page and read it over rather than joining the lists), or pass path_prefix (`app/`, `components/`, `src/pages/`) to walk one directory at a time. NEVER guess a path: if you have not seen it listed here, page or narrow until you have. CHECK can_write: when it is false this site's files are READ-ONLY here — read them and answer questions about them, but do not offer or attempt an edit, because page.patch_file and page.edit_file will refuse it. To find WHERE some words live — the date, headline or sentence a member wants changed — pass contains with a short fragment of them: only the files holding it are listed, each with match_line and match_text. Read one with page.read_file before changing it. Not for what is inside one file — that is `page.read_file`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Say what has changed on a site and where it stands now — 'what did you change?', 'what have we got saved?', 'can I go back to before that?', 'why did the last build fail?', 'what version is this on?'. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. It reports where the site's source stands: the checkpoint it is at (current_source_ref — every edit is made from it), the ledger of checkpoints newest first with each one's build status and revision, and the newest build with its failure log tail when it failed. A checkpoint is made by every page.patch_file call and by the member's save; use this to name a checkpoint for page.rollback, a revision for page.republish_revision, or to read why the last build failed. Not for undoing a change — that is `page.rollback`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Answer 'is my domain live yet?' for a page — 'is my domain working', 'why isn't my domain connected', 'check my domain again'. Every address the page holds comes back with the domains card's state (Live, Waiting for record, Issuing certificate or Needs attention) and, when something is wrong, a reason that says why; relay the state and the reason in the member's words, and call a name connected only when its state is Live. A custom domain still settling is re-checked on the spot and the check is recorded, so checked_at is the time of this answer; if rechecked is false for a domain, say the state is the last one we recorded. It only reads and costs nothing. Not for a Goosy Grow domain use such as mail or links — that is `domain.status`.

If rebuild_queued comes back false, do NOT say the pixel has stopped firing — the override is stored but no new build is on its way. post.description:
Bring in a site the member already built somewhere else — 'import my existing site', 'I have a zip of my site', 'pull in the one I built in Webflow'. It takes a public https:// link to a .zip — either a finished build or a project we compile. Give it a site_id to replace an existing site, or leave it out to create a new one. It does NOT publish: say the site was imported, not that it is live. A private, local or metadata address is refused, and so is http:// — relay that refusal rather than retrying. If findings come back, they are advisory notes about search/AI discovery, never a failure of the import. The import_report says what we detected, what came across, what we changed to host it and what could not be brought over: relay those lists, never summarise them away. While import_report.status is "compiling" the site is still being built, so page_count is not yet the answer. Not for building a new site from scratch — that is `page.create`.

post.description:
Build the site again and say what the build reports — 'try building it again', 'build it now', 'did that fix the build?', 'run it again and see if it works'. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. It builds the site's current checkpoint on the rail again — after a build failed for a reason you have fixed, or to re-run one. Every page.patch_file already builds, so you rarely need this. The tool waits a short while: a build that finishes in time answers with its outcome, and a FAILED build answers with the failing step's log tail — read it and fix the file it names. A build still running answers still_running: true with its run id; the member's editor shows the log as it lands, and page.checkpoint reports the outcome later. Not for reading why the last build failed without re-running it — that is `page.checkpoint`.

post.description:
Undo a change to the site the member is working on — 'undo that', 'put it back how it was', 'I liked it better before', 'take that last change back', 'go back to before the build broke'. Every applied edit leaves a checkpoint, so this is the undo for anything that changed the site's source. This is the member's own working copy. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. It restores the site's DRAFT source to a previous checkpoint and rebuilds — the undo for a page.patch_file (name its base_source_ref) or for any checkpoint in page.checkpoint's ledger. The live site is untouched; the preview follows the rebuild. The checkpoint left behind stays in the ledger, so a rollback can itself be rolled back. A checkpoint whose archive is gone is refused; relay that and offer another. Not for the live site visitors see — that is `page.republish_revision`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Make a brand-new website — 'build me a site for my consultancy', 'I need a landing page', 'make a website for the new product'. Create a multi-page website from a blueprint — home, about and contact with working navigation and the full search/AI discovery file set. Describe what the site is for with intent, or leave it out to get starter copy with no paid generation. When the member asked for the site themselves in this conversation it creates it at once — report what the result says; only a site nobody asked for raises its approval card first, which is the member's confirmation, and then it can still be refused. It does NOT publish either: the site is built, not put on the internet, and if build_run_id is missing say the build has not started yet — quoting build_enqueue_error as the reason when it is present, and offering to try the build again. If draft_error comes back and source_ref does not, NOTHING WAS DRAFTED: the site exists and is openable but empty, so say exactly that, quote the reason, and offer to try again ON THAT site_id — never call page.create a second time for the same request, which would leave the member with two pages. Not for changing a site that already exists — that is `page.edit`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

post.description:
Change something on a site by writing its FILES — 'add more space between these cards', 'change the button text to Book a call', 'fix the typo in the footer', 'make the hero heading bigger'. This is the one way every site whose files we hold is changed, however it was made or brought in: copy, styling, layout, a component, a page. Read each file with page.read_file first — start from the selected element's file and line when the turn gives them, or from page.edit's `located`, or find the words with page.list_files and `contains` — and copy `find` text exactly; a hunk that matches nowhere or more than once refuses the whole call and nothing is written. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. One call is ONE saved version, so send a whole change in one call. While a live workbench is showing the site the change appears there in place and no build runs (the result says build_deferred; relay its build_hint); otherwise a build follows and takes a minute or two. The result is the diff (say what it shows, never more), the new source_ref and base_source_ref (page.rollback to it undoes this). Which directories are editable depends on the project: refusals name the reason, so relay them rather than retrying. Dependency manifests and lockfiles, build configuration, generated files, and anything under a build or tooling directory are always refused. A site whose files are READ-ONLY here is refused — page.list_files reports can_write: false for one, so check that before composing a patch. A change the member asked for in this conversation is written at once; only a change nobody asked for — or any change, when the member has asked to see each one first — raises its approval card, which is the member's confirmation, and is not made, saved or built unless they approve it there. Not for rewriting whole named files from an instruction — that is `page.edit_file`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Rework whole named files of a site when the change is bigger than a couple of exact lines — 'redo the pricing section in the code', 'rewrite this component', 'change the hero copy in Hero.astro', 'restructure that page's markup'. This is the CODE path — the member is working on the actual files and names them; when they only describe a change and never name a file, use page.edit instead. No site id is needed — it works on the site the member has open on screen. It has the coding model change the named files from an instruction — page.edit scoped to those files. Use it when a change is more than a few exact lines you could patch yourself: the model reads the named files whole, rewrites them, and the build follows (unless a live workbench is showing the site — then no build runs and the result says build_deferred; relay its build_hint); only the named files may change. Include src/data/site.json in paths when the change is copy, the page list or a lead form (they live in the content model); toolchain and generated files are refused. This tool authors through a content model (`src/data/site.json`), which a site's files carry only when it was made from one of our templates; on any other tree it answers pages.edit_in_files — then make the same change with page.patch_file in this turn and say nothing to the member about the difference. A site whose files are READ-ONLY here is refused too. The result is one checkpoint (page.rollback undoes it) and the model's own one-line summary — relay that, never more. When the member asked for the rewrite themselves in this conversation it runs at once — relay its summary. Only a rewrite nobody asked for — or any rewrite, when the member has asked to see each change first — raises its approval card, which is the member's confirmation, and is not made unless they approve it there. Not for a change of a few exact lines — that is `page.patch_file`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Put a site live at a chosen time instead of now — 'publish it on Monday morning', 'schedule this to go live at 9am', 'put it up next Tuesday'. Schedule a page to publish at a chosen time. Send `at` as an ISO-8601 timestamp WITH its UTC offset, resolved against the member's own timezone. It must be at least five minutes away and within the next year. This is a public, consequential act. Call it on the ask: it raises the approval card showing the page's name, its address and the time being committed to, which is the member's confirmation. Never say a page is scheduled unless the result says it is. If `replaced` is true, say you moved an existing schedule rather than adding a second one. Not for publishing right now — that is `page.publish`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Give the member a private link so they can show a site to someone before it goes live — 'send me a link I can share', 'can my client see this first?', 'I want to show someone before publishing'. Issue a shareable preview link for a page — an unguessable, expiring URL that shows one revision WITHOUT publishing it. Nothing goes live and no address changes. Give the member the whole url immediately and say when it expires: it is shown once and cannot be looked up again. If the revision is not the live one, say so. post.description:
Let one person past a site's password without telling them the password — 'let my client in without the password', 'send them a private way in', 'give this one person access'. Mint a private link that lets one person past a page's password without knowing it. Only works on a page that HAS a password. Give the member the whole url immediately and say when it expires: it is shown once and cannot be looked up again. Setting or clearing the password kills it. Not for a preview of a version that is not live — that is `page.create_preview_link`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Say which brands ONE way: the specific brands they picked, every brand of a business type, or every brand set up from one template. Change a named group of brands — 'rename that group', 'add the new brand to my north america group', 'retire that group'.  Rename a named group of brands, change which brands it covers, change the brand answer it remembers for next time, or retire it. Get the setId from workspace_sets.list. Renaming changes only what people READ — anything already pointed at the set keeps working. The operator sees an approve card naming every new value before anything changes: call it ONCE — never call it again to 'confirm', because the card is the confirmation. Requires the sharing permission (Owner/Admin by default). Not for naming a new group — that is `workspace_sets.create`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

anyOf.description: Exactly ONE of: {workspace_ids:[...]} the brands they picked · {company_type:'...'} every brand of that business type · {template_links_of:'<template brand id>'} every brand set up from that template.

post.description:
Draw this short's beats — 'write the beats for this short', 'storyboard this short' — four to six beats with their full sheets. This is a short's script and its storyboard in ONE act: there is no separate script step. It writes the WORDS and the sheets; it does NOT draw the pictures — `shorts.mint_stills` does that, and it asks first. Show the person what it drew, let them change it, and offer the pictures. If they say 'this short' and name no id, call it with the id of the short whose board they are on. ⚠️ IT MAY ALSO CARRY `questions` — real facts the short needs and nobody has given (a name, the product, one number). When it does, ASK THEM AS YOUR VERY NEXT TURN, in your own words, in one message, and NEVER answer one yourself: a made-up name ships in the finished short. THIS TOOL CANNOT RECORD THEIR ANSWERS — send what they say to `videos.answer_script_facts` with the `key` it gave you, and call this one again only once the answers are recorded. The beats already carry a blank everywhere an answer belongs. Not for the pictures — that is `shorts.mint_stills`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Never ask which video, and never say a video is out of reach, before trying that.

post.description:
Write and save the destination copy for every place this video is set to ship — 'write the titles and descriptions for this video', 'draft the copy for YouTube and TikTok'. Write the destination copy (titles, descriptions, tags, …) for every destination this video unit is set to ship to, and save it. The destinations must already be chosen — if none are, this refuses and the operator picks them on the Ship step first. Fields the operator edited by hand are left alone. Calling it raises the approval card, which is the operator's confirmation, so call it on the ask. Not for choosing where the video ships — that is `video_unit.set_destinations`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Set what new work starts from by default — 'make vertical the default for videos', 'new emails should start as newsletters', 'change the default thumbnail style'.  Set ONE of the workspace's generation defaults — the video format, render mode, thumbnail profile or email type new work starts from. Admin only; the action refuses anyone below that role. post.description:
Save a new writing voice, or update one that already exists — 'save this as a new writing voice', 'update our casual voice'. Create or update one NAMED writing voice — an alternate to the house voice, stating only what it changes. Omit voice_id to create; pass one from writing_voices.list to update. Never restate the house voice: anything left unstated is inherited. The member sees an approve card for it before it runs; never say it is saved unless the result says it is. Not for removing a voice — that is `writing_voices.delete`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

name.description: What this voice is called — the label it is picked by. Unique within the workspace.

note.description: When to use this voice, in one line. An empty string clears it; omit it to leave it alone.

tone_primary.description: The tone words this voice leads with (e.g. urgent, direct). Omit to leave the stored list alone; pass an empty array to clear it.

rules_md.description: Free-text rules for this voice, in the operator's own words. An empty string clears it; omit it to leave it alone.

traits.description: The voice-trait table, REPLACED WHOLE when passed — a trait is a row, not a bag of fields, so send the complete list you want or omit it entirely. An empty array clears it.

tone_spectrum.description: Tone by SITUATION, REPLACED WHOLE when passed — same rule as traits. An empty array clears it.

delta.description: What this voice states DIFFERENTLY from the house voice. Anything left unstated is INHERITED from the house voice at generation time — that is the point of a named voice, so never restate the house voice here.

post.description:
Read the member their weekly briefing — 'what's my briefing say?', 'how was the week?', 'what should I be looking at?'.  Read this workspace's weekly briefing — the headline, the story, what went well, what to watch, and the moves it proposed. Call this before answering any question about the week's briefing or what it suggested; never guess it, and never invent a number it does not carry. Not for last week's raw numbers — that is `week_metrics.read`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Write the briefing again from scratch — 'redo my briefing', 'that briefing is out of date, refresh it', 'write this week's one again'.  Rewrite a briefing from scratch — this week's by default, or a past week's when week_of names one. Use it only when the person explicitly asks for a fresh one — it is limited to once a day per workspace, and the briefing already refreshes on its own every Monday. Not for reading the briefing as it stands — that is `briefing.read`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Record that the member wants to do one of the briefing's suggested moves — 'yes, let's do that one', 'I'll take that suggestion', 'do the thing the briefing suggested'.  Record that the person wants to DO one of the briefing's suggested moves. It logs the decision — which next week's briefing reads, so it stops re-proposing what they already handled — and hands you the move's own words. Doing the work itself is the relevant capability's own tool; this never publishes, spends or changes anything on its own. Not for turning a suggestion down — that is `suggestion.dismiss`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Say what we know about one customer — 'who is this lead?', 'what's the story with that contact?', 'have we talked to them before?'.  Read one customer's record — who they are, which ways exist to reach them, their tags, whether we may message them, and their recent history. Address them by their id, or by ONE key you already hold from the conversation (an email, a phone number, a Messenger id). It deliberately returns no addresses or phone numbers, and there is no way to list customers with it. The summary is small on purpose; ask for section timeline or notes when it says more exists. Not for writing on their record — that is `contact.note`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

identity_value.description: The key exactly as you observed it. It is normalised before it is looked up, so capitals in an address are fine — but a phone number without its country code cannot be matched and will be refused rather than guessed at.

identity_scope.description: The Meta PAGE id the key was seen on. REQUIRED for meta_psid and ig_id — those ids are only unique within one page, so without it nothing can be matched. Leave it out for every other kind.

section.description: Which part to read. summary (the default) is the record plus the newest few history rows and notes; timeline is the recent history only; notes is their notes only. Ask for timeline or notes when the summary says more exists.

post.description:
Attach an email, phone number or handle you hold to the right customer — 'that's the same person as this lead', 'add this email to their record', 'this number belongs to them'.  Attach a key you hold from a conversation — an email, a phone number, a Messenger id — to a customer, or take one off again. Calling it shows the operator an approve card naming the change first, and nothing is written unless they approve it themselves. You cannot approve it for them, and never pass confirm_token. Keys are matched exactly, never on a likeness, and one that already belongs to somebody else is refused rather than moved. Not for looking a customer up — that is `contact.get`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

contact_id.description: The customer this key belongs to. Read them with contact.get first — never a guess at who a key belongs to.

identity_kind.description: Which kind of key this is: an email address, a phone number, a Messenger id (meta_psid), an Instagram id (ig_id), a CRM record id (ghl_contact_id), or a Google reviewer id.

identity_value.description: The key exactly as you observed it. It is normalised before it is looked up, so capitals in an address are fine — but a phone number without its country code cannot be matched and will be refused rather than guessed at.

identity_scope.description: The Meta PAGE id the key was seen on. REQUIRED for meta_psid and ig_id — those ids are only unique within one page, so without it nothing can be matched. Leave it out for every other kind.

action.description: `link` attaches the key to that customer; `unlink` takes it off again. Both are recorded on their history.

post.description:
Mark a lead's reply as approved so it is ready to answer — 'approve that one', 'this one's good to go back', 'yes, that reply is fine'.  Mark a pending lead reply as approved, so it is ready to be answered. This is an internal review state — the lead sees nothing and is not contacted. post.description:
Check whether this account has signed the advertising authorization — 'have we signed the ad authorization', 'why can't we set up ad accounts'. Read whether this account has signed the advertising authorization — the written go-ahead we need before asking any advertising platform for access to their ad account. Call this whenever ad-account setup will not proceed, or when asked what we are authorized to do with their advertising. YOU CANNOT SIGN IT: signing is a person reading the document and typing their name on the Connections surface, and there is no tool for it — say what is missing and point them there. Not for the ad-account setup steps themselves — that is `connections.ad_account_status`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Check whether Google Business Profile is connected and can actually post right now — 'can we post to our Google Business Profile', 'why won't a local post go out'. Report whether this workspace's Google Business Profile is connected AND whether a local post can actually go out right now. Read this BEFORE offering to publish: a Business Profile can be perfectly connected while the Business Profile API still allows zero requests, because Google has not yet approved our platform's API access application — a wait on us, not on the operator. Never tell the operator to reconnect when that is the reason. Not for publishing the local post — that is `connections.publish_local_post`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Mark one guided setup step as done — because the OPERATOR SAID THEY DID IT, as in 'I've done that step' or 'I added you as a partner' — and advance to the next. Only call this when they have told you they finished that step; it records their word, and we have no way to check it for them. Nothing is sent to the platform. One step per platform also asks for the operator's own ad account id — pass `external_account_id` there, and ask them for it if you do not have it. Call connections.ad_account_status first to see what is outstanding. There is NO tool that un-marks a step: if they need to redo one, tell them to open Connections and use “Start the steps again”, which re-opens the setup without losing the steps they already finished. Not for checking whether the access actually came through — that is `connections.check_ad_account_access`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

parameters.description: Your own id for this request, echoed back and recorded on the audit trail. 1–128 characters from `A–Z a–z 0–9 . _ : -`, starting with a letter or digit; anything else is replaced by a generated id.

platform.description: Which advertising platform's ad account to set up on that platform's own account — the customer owns the account and grants us access to it. The allowed values are the enum's; do not offer a platform outside it.

step_key.description: The step to mark, taken VERBATIM from connections.ad_account_status' `steps` list. It is verified against the platform's own step catalog before anything is stored, so an invented or stale key refuses rather than being recorded.

external_account_id.description: The operator's OWN ad account id, on the ONE step that asks for it (on TikTok, 'Come back and confirm' asks for the advertiser ID). Pass it only when they have told you the id; any other step refuses it rather than silently dropping it. NEVER pass a password, token or API key here; this field is an account identifier only.

post.description:
See which conversions Google Analytics tracks for this brand — 'what conversions can we report on', 'which conversions are we showing now'. Read the conversions the connected Google Analytics property tracks and which of them this brand currently reports. Call this before answering anything about conversion reporting, and before changing the reported set — never guess the available list. Read `availability` first: it distinguishes a brand with no Google Analytics connection from conversion reporting being temporarily unreadable, and those are different things to tell the operator. Not for changing the reported set — that is `connections.set_conversion_events`.

Check how a member's own MCP server or API address wants to sign in, before they set it up — 'check this API address before I add it', 'does this connector need a token'. Ask a member's own MCP server or API address how it signs in, BEFORE they set it up. Use it when the operator says they want to bring their own connector and gives you an address: it dials the address once, reads nothing but the way it refuses, and reports whether it wants a token, a sign-in with the provider, or nothing at all. It writes no row, stores no credential and registers nothing — finishing the setup is the operator's own act in Connections → Add custom connector, because the token they may need to paste is a value no tool may ever carry. post.description:
Get this workspace its own texting number — 'buy us a texting number', 'get a phone number for SMS'. Buy a texting number for this workspace. It SPENDS MONEY — a number carries a recurring monthly charge — so calling it raises the approval card naming the number and its monthly charge, which is the operator's confirmation, and it buys only on their approve. Pass the exact number the operator chose. Buying a number does NOT make texting work: the number lands in `compliance_pending` and the operator still has to register it with the phone companies, which is a step only they can do. Say that when you offer it. Not for why texts cannot go out — that is `connections.messaging_registration_status`. Over the API it answers in two calls: without confirmation_id it proposes — says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes, spends and sends nothing; the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key, do it.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

phone_number.description: The number to buy, in full international format. It must be one the operator has chosen from the available list — never one you composed, and never a number the operator merely mentioned in passing.

confirmation_id.description: Omit to propose: the first call says what would happen, returns a confirmation_id and changes nothing. To go ahead, send the same arguments again with that confirmation_id, on a member's own API key; a service account's key can propose but never confirm.

post.description:
Begin or resume the guided setup for connecting a brand's own ad account — 'help me connect our ad account', 'walk me through ad account setup'. Begin or resume the guided setup that gets us access to this brand's own ad account on one platform, and return the next step. Safe to call when setup is already under way — it RESUMES and never resets progress. Nothing is sent to the platform and nothing is spent; this only opens the guided steps the operator then performs in the platform's own tools. Not for marking one step done — that is `connections.complete_ad_account_step`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

Omit it when they are making a new account — that is the normal case and the walkthrough collects it later. NEVER pass a password, token or API key here; this field is an account identifier only.

post.description:
Check how many clicks this brand's tracked links have had — 'how many clicks did this link get', 'how did this campaign's links perform'. Read how many clicks this brand's tracked links have had — for one piece, one campaign, this week, or the whole brand. Returns a sentence you can say as-is plus the rows behind it, and `goes_out_on` / `domain_is_ours`, which tell you whether this brand's links are riding the platform's name or the brand's own. Call this before answering any question about clicks; never guess a number. Not for making a new tracked link — that is `links.shorten`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.

post.description:
Move this brand's tracked links onto a domain the customer owns — 'use our own domain for tracked links', 'check if our link domain is set up yet'. Put this brand's tracked links on a domain the customer owns — for the whole account or for one brand — and check on one that is still being set up. Pass the ROOT domain they own (northwindcoffee.com); the links. prefix is added for them. If we hold the domain we add the record ourselves and it is live in about a minute; otherwise the answer carries the one record they add wherever their domain lives, and `action: "check"` with the returned id looks for it. Links already out there keep working either way. Not for connecting a domain to a site — that is `domain.connect`.

Every result names the workspace it ran in. Say which workspace the answer is about. When the account has more than one workspace and none is selected, this tool refuses with `workspace_ambiguous` and lists the choices — offer them, never pick one.
